behavioral_notes.observation: The whole module pivots on this method. It first auto-runs compute_landed_cost for any cost lacking valuation_adjustment_lines, then _check_sum guards that each cost line's distributed amounts re-sum to its price_unit (else UserError 'recompute the landed costs'). For each valuation adjustment line whose product has valuation=='real_time' it builds an account.move (move_type='entry') of paired debit/credit lines via line._create_accounting_entries(remaining_qty), creates+posts that journal entry (move._post()), flips state draft->done, and finally calls valuation_adjustment_lines.move_id._set_value() so the underlying stock.move/stock valuation layer absorbs the extra cost. Products with manual (periodic) valuation are skipped for the journal entry but still adjust cost. Validation is irreversible: button_cancel raises on done records ('create negative landed costs to reverse them').

The split engine. It deletes prior stock.valuation.adjustment.lines, then for every targeted stock.move x every cost_line creates a valuation adjustment line and accumulates totals (total_qty/weight/volume/cost/line-count). For each cost line it allocates price_unit across moves by split_method: 'equal' = price_unit/line-count; 'by_quantity' = quantity x (price_unit/total_qty); 'by_weight' = weight x (price_unit/total_weight); 'by_volume' = volume x (price_unit/total_volume); 'by_current_cost_price' = former_cost x (price_unit/total_cost). Each share is HALF-UP rounded to currency precision and any residual rounding_diff (price_unit - sum of splits) is added back to the largest line so the totals reconcile exactly. Result is written to additional_landed_cost on each adjustment line. split_method defaults come from product.template.split_method_landed_cost.

_get_targeted_move_ids returns picking_ids.move_ids, i.e. the stock moves of the linked receipt transfer(s). get_valuation_lines walks those moves and, ONLY for products whose cost_method is 'fifo' or 'average' (real cost) with a non-cancel state and nonzero qty, captures former_cost = move._get_value() plus weight/volume = product.weight/volume * received qty. Products on standard costing are rejected with a UserError. This is the explicit binding from an extra cost back to the specific inbound stock.move it must inflate.

behavioral_notes.element: account.move.button_create_landed_costs / landed_costs_ids (link to the vendor bill)
behavioral_notes.observation: stock_landed_costs inherits account.move: button_create_landed_costs spawns a stock.landed.cost from a vendor bill (move_type in_invoice/in_refund), copying each account.move.line flagged is_landed_costs_line into a cost_line (product, expense account, company-currency price_subtotal, split_method), and opens its form. is_landed_costs_line is set when product.template.landed_cost_ok is true (also stamped on purchase.order.line._prepare_account_move_line and account.move.line onchange). vendor_bill_id on the landed cost closes the loop, and landed_costs_visible drives the bill's 'Create Landed Costs' smart button. This is how freight/duty invoiced on a separate vendor bill is routed onto an earlier receipt.

_create_accounting_entries picks debit = product stock_valuation account, credit = cost line's account_id (fallback cost product expense), erroring if no expense account is configured. _create_account_move_line scales the posted amount by remaining_qty/quantity (only what is still in stock is capitalised; already-sold qty hits COGS) and reverses debit/credit for negative (corrective) costs. On the inventory side, stock.move._get_value_from_extra adds each done landed cost's additional_landed_cost into the move's accounting value and appends a human-readable '+ amount from <vendor bill> (Landed Cost: ...)' breakdown, so the stock valuation layer and the GL stay in lockstep.

No frontend assets: 0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry registrations, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The UI is pure server-rendered form/list/kanban XML (3 form, 4 list, 1 kanban, 1 search) plus the 'Create Landed Costs' smart button injected on the account.move (vendor bill) form. No client-side widgets are added by this module.

classification.rationale: stock_landed_costs is an inventory-valuation / cost-accounting support extension, not a primary value-creating activity. It does not move goods (that is stock, value-model chain); it corrects the *book value* of received goods by capitalising freight/duties/insurance into inventory cost and writing the matching debit-stock-valuation / credit-expense journal entry into the financial ledger (account.move). That is firm-infrastructure cost accounting, a Porter support activity, classified support/support. It sits squarely under APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -> 9.x Perform general accounting and reporting: it feeds inventory valuation (cf. account 9.2/9.5) by adjusting product cost and posting the revaluation entry, bridging the stock valuation layer (stock_account) and the GL. It is the cost-accounting complement to the receipt (4.0 Deliver Physical Products) rather than a logistics step itself.

Per-product valuation adjustment lines (former / additional / new value) with exact-total rounding

Eligibility limited to FIFO/average-costed, real-time-valuated products

No anglo-saxon/continental nuance beyond debit stock valuation / credit expense; bespoke duty-deferral or split-by-customs-value rules need development
No multi-currency landed-cost line revaluation beyond company-currency conversion at bill rate
Reversal is manual (negative landed cost), no one-click undo
